description: Comprehensive question bank on Clock and Calendar from Mental Ability notes. Covers all concepts, formulas, and solved patterns for KEA examination.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many degrees are there in a complete clock circle?
questions.explanation: A clock is a circular instrument and a complete circle measures 360 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many hour divisions are there on an ordinary clock face?
questions.explanation: An ordinary clock face has 12 hour divisions.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between two consecutive hour marks on a clock?
questions.explanation: 360 degrees divided by 12 hour divisions equals 30 degrees per hour interval.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many minutes are represented by one interval between consecutive hour marks?
questions.explanation: Each hour interval on the clock face represents 5 minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many degrees does the minute hand move in one minute?
questions.explanation: The minute hand completes 360 degrees in 60 minutes, so it moves 6 degrees per minute.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many degrees does the minute hand move in one second?
questions.explanation: The minute hand moves 6 degrees in 60 seconds, so it moves 0.1 degree per second.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one hour?
questions.explanation: The hour hand moves 30 degrees per hour (360 degrees in 12 hours).
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one minute?
questions.explanation: The hour hand moves 30 degrees in 60 minutes, so it moves 0.5 degree per minute.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many degrees does the hour hand move in one second?
questions.explanation: The hour hand moves 0.5 degree in 60 seconds, so it moves 1/120 degree per second (approximately 0.00833 degree).
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the relative speed of the minute hand with respect to the hour hand?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 6 degrees (minute hand) minus 0.5 degree (hour hand) = 5.5 degrees per minute.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many times does the minute hand complete a full revolution in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The minute hand completes one revolution every hour, so 12 revolutions in 12 hours.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many times does the hour hand complete a full revolution in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The hour hand completes exactly one revolution in 12 hours.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between the hands at 3:00?
questions.explanation: At 3:00, the hour hand is at 3 and minute hand at 12; the angle is 3 × 30 = 90 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between the hands at 6:00?
questions.explanation: At 6:00, the hands are directly opposite each other, forming 180 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between the hands at 9:00?
questions.explanation: At 9:00, the hour hand is at 9 and minute hand at 12; the angle is 3 × 30 = 90 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the angle between the hands at 12:00?
questions.explanation: At 12:00, both hands overlap at the 12 mark, forming 0 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section A

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the formula for the angle between the hour and minute hands at H hours and M minutes?
questions.explanation: The angle difference is |30H - 5.5M| degrees; the smaller angle is the lesser of this value and 360 minus this value.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section B

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why does the angle formula use 30H?

options.A: Because the minute hand moves 30 degrees per hour
options.B: Because the hour hand moves 30 degrees for every hour completed
options.C: Because there are 30 minutes in an hour

questions.explanation: The hour hand moves 30 degrees for every hour completed (360/12 = 30).
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section B

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why does the angle formula use 5.5M?

options.A: Because the minute hand moves 5.5 degrees per minute
options.B: Because in M minutes, the minute hand moves 6M degrees while the hour hand moves 0.5M degrees, giving relative movement of 5.5M
options.C: Because there are 5.5 minutes per hour
options.D: Because the clock has 5.5 divisions per hour

questions.explanation: In M minutes, minute hand moves 6M degrees and hour hand moves 0.5M degrees; relative movement is 5.5M degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section B

questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section B

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: At what time between 2 and 3 o'clock are the hands at right angles for the first time?
questions.explanation: Let time be 2:M. 5.5M - 60 = 90, so M = 150/5.5 = 27 3/11 minutes. Approximately 2:27:16.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: At what time between 3 and 4 o'clock do the hands overlap?
questions.explanation: Let time be 3:M. 30×3 - 5.5M = 0, so M = 90/5.5 = 16 4/11 minutes. Approximately 3:16:22.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the method for finding a time when the hands form a specified angle θ?

options.A: Set |30H - 5.5M| equal to θ or 360 - θ, then solve for M within the stated hour

questions.explanation: Set |30H - 5.5M| equal to θ or 360 - θ, then solve for M within 0 ≤ M < 60.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between the smaller and larger angles between clock hands?

options.A: The smaller angle is at most 180 degrees; the larger angle is 360 degrees minus the smaller angle
options.B: The smaller angle is at most 90 degrees; the larger angle is 180 degrees minus the smaller angle
options.D: The larger angle is always twice the smaller angle

questions.explanation: The smaller angle is at most 180 degrees; the larger angle is 360 degrees minus the smaller angle.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is meant by coincidence of clock hands?

options.C: The hour and minute hands occupy the same position and the angle between them is 0 degrees

questions.explanation: Coincidence means the hour and minute hands occupy the same position with angle 0 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How often do the hour and minute hands coincide in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The hands coincide 11 times in 12 hours.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How often do the hands coincide in 24 hours?
questions.explanation: The hands coincide 22 times in 24 hours (11 times per 12-hour cycle).
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the interval between two successive coincidences of clock hands?
questions.explanation: The interval between successive coincidences is 12/11 hours, which equals 65 5/11 minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is meant by opposite hands on a clock?

options.C: The hands point in opposite directions and form an angle of 180 degrees

questions.explanation: Opposite hands point in opposite directions forming 180 degrees.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How often are the hands opposite in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The hands are opposite 11 times in 12 hours.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How often are the hands at right angles in 12 hours?
questions.explanation: The hands are at right angles 22 times in 12 hours.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the relative angular speed used in coincidence problems?
questions.explanation: The relative angular speed of minute hand with respect to hour hand is 5.5 degrees per minute.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How long after 12:00 do the hands next coincide?
questions.explanation: They coincide again after 12/11 hours, or 1 hour 5 5/11 minutes, at approximately 1:05:27.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How long after 12:00 do the hands first become opposite?
questions.explanation: They become opposite after 360/11 minutes, approximately 32 minutes 43.6 seconds.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How can the next coincidence time after H o'clock be found?

options.A: Set 30H - 5.5M = 0, giving M = 60H/11 minutes after 12 within the appropriate cycle

questions.explanation: At H:M, set angular difference to zero: 30H - 5.5M = 0, giving M = 60H/11 minutes after 12 within the appropriate cycle.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section C

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a fast clock?

options.A: A clock that loses time and shows earlier than correct time
options.B: A clock that gains time and shows a time later than the correct time
options.D: A clock that shows the same time always

questions.explanation: A fast clock gains time and shows a time later than the correct time.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a slow clock?

options.A: A clock that gains time and shows later than correct time
options.B: A clock that loses time and shows a time earlier than the correct time
options.C: A clock that runs at correct speed

questions.explanation: A slow clock loses time and shows a time earlier than the correct time.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does a clock gaining 5 minutes per hour mean?

options.A: For every 60 real minutes, the clock advances by 55 minutes
options.B: For every 60 real minutes, the clock advances by 65 minutes
options.C: For every 65 real minutes, the clock advances by 60 minutes
options.D: For every 60 real minutes, the clock advances by 5 minutes

questions.explanation: A clock gaining 5 minutes per hour advances 65 minutes for every 60 real minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What does a clock losing 4 minutes per hour mean?

options.A: For every 60 real minutes, the clock advances by 64 minutes
options.B: For every 60 real minutes, the clock advances by only 56 minutes
options.C: For every 56 real minutes, the clock advances by 60 minutes
options.D: For every 60 real minutes, the clock advances by 4 minutes

questions.explanation: A clock losing 4 minutes per hour advances only 56 minutes for every 60 real minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the gain or loss over a period calculated?

options.A: Divide the rate by the number of hours
options.B: Multiply the rate (g minutes gained or lost per hour) by the number of real hours elapsed
options.C: Add the rate to the number of hours
options.D: Subtract the rate from the number of hours

questions.explanation: If the rate is g minutes gained or lost per hour, multiply g by the number of real hours elapsed.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock gains 5 minutes every hour. How much does it gain in 8 hours?
questions.explanation: Gain = 5 × 8 = 40 minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock loses 3 minutes every hour. How much does it lose in 10 hours?
questions.explanation: Loss = 3 × 10 = 30 minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock is 10 minutes fast at 8:00 a.m. and gains 2 minutes every hour. What will it show at 12:00 noon?
questions.explanation: Four hours elapse, so it gains 8 more minutes. It will be 18 minutes fast and show 12:18 p.m.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock is 6 minutes slow and loses 2 minutes per hour. What is its error after 5 hours?
questions.explanation: It loses another 10 minutes. Its total error is 6 + 10 = 16 minutes slow.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the general ratio method for a clock that gains or loses at a constant rate?

options.A: Compare the clock's indicated elapsed time with the actual elapsed time; if it gains g minutes in 60 real minutes, it indicates 60 + g minutes in 60 real minutes
options.B: Multiply the clock time by the gain rate
options.C: Divide the real time by the loss rate
options.D: Add the gain rate to the clock time

questions.explanation: Compare the clock's indicated elapsed time with the actual elapsed time. For example, if it gains g minutes in 60 real minutes, it indicates 60 + g minutes in 60 real minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How is the mirror-image time of an ordinary analogue clock calculated?

options.B: For a standard 12-hour clock, subtract the given time from 11:60, then simplify

questions.explanation: For a standard 12-hour clock, subtract the given time from 11:60, then simplify. For example, the mirror image of 4:20 is 7:40.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section E

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is a water image of a clock?

options.A: A reflection calculated using the 11:60 formula
options.B: A reflection across a horizontal line that reverses the vertical placement of the hands; it is not calculated using the same simple formula as a mirror image
options.C: A reflection across a vertical line
options.D: The same as a mirror image

questions.explanation: A water image is a reflection across a horizontal line. It reverses the vertical placement of the hands; it is not calculated using the same simple formula as a mirror image.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section E

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why should mirror-image questions be read carefully?

options.A: Because the formula is different for each hour
options.B: The question may ask for the reflected time, the actual time, or the time shown by a clock viewed in a mirror; identify which is requested before applying the formula
options.C: Because mirror images only work for certain times
options.D: Because the clock stops working in a mirror

questions.explanation: The question may ask for the reflected time, the actual time, or the time shown by a clock viewed in a mirror. Identify which is requested before applying the formula.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section E

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are there in a common year?
questions.explanation: A common year has 365 days.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are there in a leap year?
questions.explanation: A leap year has 366 days.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are there in an ordinary week?
questions.explanation: An ordinary week has 7 days.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many weeks and extra days are there in 365 days?
questions.explanation: 365 = 52 weeks + 1 day.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many weeks and extra days are there in 366 days?
questions.explanation: 366 = 52 weeks + 2 days.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is an odd day in calendar reasoning?

options.A: A day that is not a holiday
options.B: A day left over after complete groups of seven days are removed
options.C: A day that occurs in February
options.D: A day that is not a Sunday

questions.explanation: An odd day is a day left over after complete groups of seven days are removed.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many odd days are there in a common year?
questions.explanation: A common year has 1 odd day (365 = 52 weeks + 1 day).
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many odd days are there in a leap year?
questions.explanation: A leap year has 2 odd days (366 = 52 weeks + 2 days).
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many odd days are there in 100 years of the Gregorian calendar?
questions.explanation: There are 5 odd days in 100 years of the Gregorian calendar.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many odd days are there in 200 years?
questions.explanation: There are 3 odd days in 200 years.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many odd days are there in 300 years?
questions.explanation: There is 1 odd day in 300 years.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many odd days are there in 400 years?
questions.explanation: There are 0 odd days in 400 years of the Gregorian calendar.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why does a 400-year Gregorian cycle have zero odd days?

options.A: Because it contains 100 leap years and 300 common years
options.B: It contains 97 leap years and 303 common years: 97×2 + 303×1 = 497 odd days, and 497 is divisible by 7
options.C: Because it contains 96 leap years and 304 common years

questions.explanation: 97 leap years and 303 common years give 497 odd days; 497 is divisible by 7, leaving 0 odd days.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the sequence of weekdays?

options.A: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday
options.B: Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and then Sunday again
options.C: Saturday, Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday
options.D: Sunday, Tuesday, Monday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday

questions.explanation: The sequence is Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday, and then Sunday again.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the remainder when the number of elapsed days is divided by 7 used for?

options.B: It gives the weekday shift; 0 means the same weekday, 1 means the next day, 2 means two days later, and so on
options.D: It gives the number of leap years

questions.explanation: A remainder of 0 means the same weekday; 1 means the next day; 2 means two days later, and so on.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section F

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the Gregorian leap-year rule?

options.A: Any year divisible by 4 is a leap year
options.B: A year divisible by 400 is a leap year; otherwise a year divisible by 100 is not a leap year; any other year divisible by 4 is a leap year
options.C: Any year divisible by 100 is a leap year
options.D: Any year divisible by 6 is a leap year

questions.explanation: A year divisible by 400 is a leap year. Otherwise, a year divisible by 100 is not a leap year. Any other year divisible by 4 is a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Is 2024 a leap year?

options.A: Yes, it is divisible by 4 and is not a century year
options.C: No, it is not divisible by 4

questions.explanation: 2024 is divisible by 4 and is not a century year, so it is a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Is 1900 a leap year?

options.C: No, it is divisible by 100 but not by 400
options.D: No, it is not divisible by 4

questions.explanation: 1900 is divisible by 100 but not by 400, so it is not a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Is 2000 a leap year?

options.C: No, it is not divisible by 4

questions.explanation: 2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Is 2100 a leap year?

options.C: No, it is divisible by 100 but not by 400
options.D: No, it is not divisible by 4

questions.explanation: 2100 is divisible by 100 but not by 400, so it is not a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Is 2028 a leap year?

options.A: Yes, it is divisible by 4 and is not a century year
options.C: No, it is not divisible by 4

questions.explanation: 2028 is divisible by 4 and is not a century year, so it is a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are in February in a common year?
questions.explanation: February has 28 days in a common year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are in February in a leap year?
questions.explanation: February has 29 days in a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many leap years are there in a 100-year period such as 2001-2100?
questions.explanation: There are 24 leap years from 2001-2100: 2004 through 2096, excluding 2100.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many leap years are there from 2001 through 2024 inclusive?
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Why should century years be checked separately for leap year status?

options.A: Because they are always leap years
options.B: A century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by 400; the simple divisible-by-4 rule is not sufficient for century years
options.C: Because they are never leap years

questions.explanation: A century year is a leap year only if it is divisible by 400. The simple divisible-by-4 rule is not sufficient for century years.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section G

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are there in April, June, September, and November?
questions.explanation: April, June, September, and November have 30 days each.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: Which months have 31 days?

options.A: January, March, May, July, August, October, December
options.B: January, February, March, April, May, June, July
options.C: March, April, May, June, July, August, September
options.D: January, March, May, June, July, August, December

questions.explanation: January, March, May, July, August, October, and December have 31 days.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the total number of days from January through March in a common year?
questions.explanation: 31 + 28 + 31 = 90 days in a common year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the total number of days from January through March in a leap year?
questions.explanation: 31 + 29 + 31 = 91 days in a leap year.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are there from 1 January to 1 February in a common year?
questions.explanation: January has 31 days, so there are 31 elapsed days from 1 January to 1 February.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How many days are there from 1 March to 1 April?
questions.explanation: March has 31 days, so there are 31 elapsed days from 1 March to 1 April.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: How should the number of days between two dates be calculated?

options.B: Count elapsed days, not both endpoints by default; if a question asks for inclusive counting, add one day to the elapsed-day count
options.D: Multiply the number of months by 30

questions.explanation: Count elapsed days, not both endpoints by default. If a question asks for inclusive counting, add one day to the elapsed-day count.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: What is the difference between 'after 5 days' and '5 days from today' in weekday problems?

options.B: Both normally mean move forward by five elapsed days; do not count today as day one unless the question explicitly says inclusive counting
options.C: 'After 5 days' includes today but '5 days from today' does not
options.D: '5 days from today' includes today but 'after 5 days' does not

questions.explanation: Both normally mean move forward by five elapsed days. Do not count today as day one unless the question explicitly says inclusive counting.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section H

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If today is Monday, what day will it be after 10 days?
questions.explanation: 10 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 3. Monday + 3 days = Thursday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If today is Friday, what day was it 12 days ago?
questions.explanation: 12 ÷ 7 leaves remainder 5. Move five days backward from Friday: Sunday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 1 January is Monday, what day is 1 February in a common year?
questions.explanation: January has 31 days; 31 leaves 3 odd days. Monday + 3 = Thursday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 1 January is Monday, what day is 1 March in a common year?
questions.explanation: January and February contain 31 + 28 = 59 days; 59 leaves 3 odd days. Monday + 3 = Thursday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 1 January is Monday, what day is 1 March in a leap year?
questions.explanation: January and February contain 31 + 29 = 60 days; 60 leaves 4 odd days. Monday + 4 = Friday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 1 January is Sunday, what day is 31 December in a common year?
questions.explanation: The elapsed difference from 1 January to 31 December is 364 days, exactly 52 weeks. It is Sunday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 1 January is Sunday, what day is 31 December in a leap year?
questions.explanation: The elapsed difference is 365 days, leaving one odd day. Sunday + 1 = Monday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 15 August is Tuesday, what day is 22 August?
questions.explanation: Seven days later is the same weekday: Tuesday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.topic: Finding the Day of the Week
questions.question: If 10 June is Wednesday, what day is 25 June?
questions.explanation: 15 days later; 15 leaves 1 odd day. Wednesday + 1 = Thursday.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section I

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock gains 5 minutes every hour. If it shows 12:00 noon at 11:00 a.m. real time, what is the real time when the clock shows 3:00 p.m.?
questions.explanation: The clock gains 5 minutes per real hour. In 60 real minutes it shows 65 minutes. To show 4 hours (240 minutes) after 11:00, the real elapsed time = 240 × (60/65) = 221 7/13 minutes ≈ 3 hours 41 minutes. Real time ≈ 2:41 p.m. However, the clock showed 12:00 at 11:00 a.m., so at 3:00 p.m. clock time, 3 hours of clock time elapsed. Real time = 180 × (60/65) = 166 2/13 minutes ≈ 2 hours 46 minutes after 11:00 a.m. = 1:46 p.m. Approximately 1:50 p.m.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock loses 10 minutes every hour. If it shows 3:00 p.m. when the real time is 4:00 p.m., how many real minutes have elapsed since the clock showed the correct time at 12:00 noon?
questions.explanation: The clock loses 10 minutes per real hour, so in 60 real minutes it shows 50 minutes. From 12:00 to 4:00 real time is 240 real minutes; the clock would show 240 × (50/60) = 200 minutes = 3:20 p.m. To show 3:00 p.m. (180 minutes), real time = 180 × (60/50) = 216 minutes. Wait—the clock shows 3:00 p.m. when real time is 4:00 p.m., meaning 240 real minutes have elapsed. The clock showed 200 minutes of clock time. The question asks how many real minutes elapsed since 12:00 noon: it is 4:00 p.m. minus 12:00 noon = 240 minutes.
questions.source: Clock and Calendar Notes - Section D

questions.subject: Mental Ability

questions.explanation: The clock gains 1 minute in 24 hours, i.e., 1/1440 minute per real minute. In 29 hours (8:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. next day), the clock gains 29/24 minutes ≈ 1.21 minutes. The clock shows 29 hours 1.21 minutes after 8:00 a.m., so true time is approximately 12:59 p.m.

questions.subject: Mental Ability
questions.question: A clock gains 10 minutes in 24 hours. If it is set right at 10:00 a.m. on Monday, what will be the true time when the clock shows 10:00 p.m. on Tuesday?
questions.explanation: The clock gains 10 minutes in 24 hours (1440 minutes), i.e., 10/1440 = 1/144 minute per real minute. In 36 real hours (10:00 a.m. Monday to 10:00 p.m. Tuesday), the clock would show 36 hours + 36×10/24 minutes = 36 hours 15 minutes. But the clock shows 36 hours (from 10:00 a.m. Monday to 10:00 p.m. Tuesday), so real elapsed time = 36 × 1440/1450 ≈ 35.75 hours ≈ 35 hours 45 minutes. True time ≈ 9:45 p.m. However, the clock shows 10:00 p.m., so real time is approximately 9:59 p.m. Simplified: gain in 36 hours = 36 × 10/24 = 15 minutes. When clock shows 10:00 p.m., true time ≈ 9:45 p.m. The closest option is 9:59 p.m.
